evidence.note: Agent wrote the ENTIRE system in large up-front Write calls — db.js, broadcast.js, complete server.js (all REST/WS/auth/slash/mentions), complete irc.js, and the full SPA index.html — all before ever launching anything. No thin slice was run first; features were built blind rather than grown against a live substrate.

Only after all code was written did the agent create supervisor.js (foreground launch of 3 HTTP nodes + IRC + broadcast hub with auto-restart) and start.sh, then launch. The launcher is deliberately designed for multi-node foreground + resilience — not an afterthought — which lifts it above anchor 3.

Health checked across all three nodes and a real cross-node auth→post→read slice verified (register node0, me node1, workspace node1, post node2, read node0 with seq:1). Genuine end-to-end verification — but it happens once at the very end, not as an early continuous feedback loop.

IRC end-to-end test then cleanup and completion. The full big-bang verification pass occurs only after the whole system was authored, confirming a write-everything-then-launch pattern rather than skeleton-first.

reasoning: The agent authored every subsystem before running anything, then stood up a well-designed foreground three-node cluster with health and a verified cross-node auth→post→read slice at the very end. The launcher and health surface are deliberate and multi-node (above anchor 3's 'afterthought'), but the runnable cluster was back-loaded rather than established early, and features were not grown against a live substrate — so it falls short of anchor 5's 'reasonably early and adds features onto it.' This lands between 3 and 5, at 4.
